claim: YouTube disclosed in 2021 that it reached 2 million creators enrolled in the YouTube Partner Program, with 10 monetization methods available, but the same post gives no aggregate payout total for that population, so no per-creator average income can be derived from this source alone.
stance_target: Aggregate creator-count disclosures without an accompanying payout figure cannot establish average or median creator income
scope_conditions: Global (not US-only); YouTube Partner Program; platform first-party disclosure, 10 February 2022
quoted_support: In 2021, we reached the incredible milestone of 2 million creators in the YouTube Partner Program, with 10 ways for them to make money.

claim: More than 40% of creators who received a payment from the YouTube Shorts Fund in 2021 had not previously monetized any content on YouTube, indicating the Fund functioned partly as a new-monetization onramp rather than solely rewarding already-monetized creators.
stance_target: Some platform monetization programs expand the pool of paid creators beyond the existing Partner Program population
scope_conditions: YouTube Shorts Fund, 2021, global; no base sample size (N) disclosed for the 40% figure
quoted_support: In fact, over 40 percent of creators who got a check from the Fund last year weren't previously monetizing their content on YouTube.

claim: YouTube reported daily live watchtime more than tripled between January 2020 and December 2021, but did not disclose the absolute watch-hour figures, only the multiple.
stance_target: Platform growth claims stated as multiples without absolute baselines limit independent verification
quoted_support: daily live watchtime more than tripled between January 2020 and December 2021.
